        for c in range(w):

                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            cells = []
            while stack:
                x, y = stack.pop()
                cells.append((x, y))
                for nx, ny in ((x-1,y), (x+1,y), (x,y-1), (x,y+1)):
                    if (0 <= nx < h and 0 <= ny < w and (nx, ny) not in seen
                            and grid[nx][ny] == color):
                        seen.add((nx, ny))
                        stack.append((nx, ny))
            minr = min(x for x, y in cells)
            minc = min(y for x, y in cells)
            shape = frozenset((x-minr, y-minc) for x, y in cells)
            objects.append((color, cells, shape))

    # Identify the template color: it has a long straight marker, often
    # accompanied by another small object of the same color.
    color_scores = {}
    for color, cells, shape in objects:
        rs = Counter(x for x, y in cells)
        cs = Counter(y for x, y in cells)
        color_scores[color] = max(color_scores.get(color, 0),
                                  max(rs.values()) + max(cs.values()))
    template_color = max(color_scores, key=color_scores.get)

    # Use the most compact template object, then recolor any matching
    # object shape elsewhere to the template color.
    templates = [shape for color, cells, shape in objects
                 if color == template_color and len(cells) > 1]
    if not templates:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    template = min(templates, key=len)

    for color, cells, shape in objects:
        if color != template_color and shape == template:
            for r, c in cells:
                out[r][c] = template_color
    return out

    guide = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == guide_color]
    row_counts = Counter(r for r, c in guide)
    col_counts = Counter(c for r, c in guide)
    er = max(row_counts, key=row_counts.get)
    ec = max(col_counts, key=col_counts.get)

    # Objects are separate 4-connected components. Find the isolated object
    # lying beyond one arm of the L, while staying on the same side of the other.
    seen = set()
    objects = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color in (bg, guide_color) or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            comp = []
            while stack:
                x, y = stack.pop()
                comp.append((x, y))
                for nx, ny in ((x-1,y), (x+1,y), (x,y-1), (x,y+1)):
                    if (0 <= nx < h and 0 <= ny < w and (nx, ny) not in seen
                            and grid[nx][ny] == color):
                        seen.add((nx, ny))
                        stack.append((nx, ny))
            cr = sum(x for x, y in comp) / len(comp)
            cc0 = sum(y for x, y in comp) / len(comp)
            objects.append((cr, cc0, comp))

    # With the elbow near an edge, the target is on the other side of the
    # nearer arm; choose the closest object in that direction.
    arm_up = any(r < er and c == ec for r, c in guide)
    arm_left = any(r == er and c < ec for r, c in guide)
    arm_right = any(r == er and c > ec for r, c in guide)
    arm_down = any(r > er and c == ec for r, c in guide)

    possible = []
    if arm_up and arm_right:
        possible = [o for o in objects if o[0] > er and o[1] < ec]
    elif arm_up and arm_left:
        possible = [o for o in objects if o[0] > er]
    elif arm_down and arm_left:
        possible = [o for o in objects if o[1] > ec]
    elif arm_down and arm_right:
        possible = [o for o in objects if o[0] < er and o[1] > ec]

    if not possible:
        possible = objects
    target = min(possible, key=lambda o: abs(o[0]-er) + abs(o[1]-ec))[2] if possible else []
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r, c in target:
        out[r][c] = guide_color
    return out

def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Connected components of all non-background colors
    seen = set()
    comps = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color == bg or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            cells = []
            while stack:
                x, y = stack.pop()
                cells.append((x, y))
                for nx, ny in ((x-1,y),(x+1,y),(x,y-1),(x,y+1)):
                    if 0 <= nx < h and 0 <= ny < w and (nx,ny) not in seen and grid[nx][ny] == color:
                        seen.add((nx,ny))
                        stack.append((nx,ny))
            comps.append((color, cells))

    # The guide component is the one with the largest sum of row/column
    # spans; its long arms form an L.
    def guide_score(item):
        color, cells = item
        rs = [r for r,c in cells]
        cs = [c for r,c in cells]
        return (max(rs)-min(rs)+1) + (max(cs)-min(cs)+1)

    guide_color, guide = max(comps, key=guide_score)
    rcount = Counter(r for r,c in guide)
    ccount = Counter(c for r,c in guide)
    er = max(rcount, key=rcount.get)
    ec = max(ccount, key=ccount.get)

    # For an L with arms up and right, target down-left; choose the closest
    # other component in that opposite quadrant.
    up = sum(1 for r,c in guide if c == ec and r < er)
    down = sum(1 for r,c in guide if c == ec and r > er)
    left = sum(1 for r,c in guide if r == er and c < ec)
    right = sum(1 for r,c in guide if r == er and c > ec)
    sr = 1 if up >= down else -1
    sc = 1 if left >= right else -1

    choices = []
    for color, cells in comps:
        if color == guide_color:
            continue
        cr = sum(r for r,c in cells) / len(cells)
        cc = sum(c for r,c in cells) / len(cells)
        if (cr-er)*sr > 0 and (cc-ec)*sc > 0:
            choices.append((abs(cr-er)+abs(cc-ec), cells))

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    if choices:
        _, target = min(choices, key=lambda x: x[0])
        for r,c in target:
            out[r][c] = guide_color
    return out
